decisions.statement: The pages written are the pages of that page type and of every page type beneath that type.
Nothing here reads a page's own body.
A page type with no property under either key is refused.
A page with no value under the key read from is passed over rather than refused.
A page already with the key written to is passed over rather than refused.
A list holding one value becomes that value where the key written to has one value.
A list holding more than one value is refused where the key written to has one value.
The value is written as the body spells that value rather than as text to quote.
The key written to takes the place the key read from held.
The key read from goes with the value that key held.
A count handed in holds how many pages the value is moved on.
A run handed no count moves the value on every page with the key read from.
A count that is no whole number above nothing is refused.
One page refused refuses the whole change.
A refusal over a page names that page.
The edits are worked out by the change reached.
That change acts on a page type, as this one does.
That change is reached through the runner rather than by an import.
Nothing here works out a body of its own.
Nothing here reads the index.

definition: one key's value written under another key on every page of one page type
